title: Ministry of Heavy Industries (MHI) receives 20 bids under the Scheme to Promote Manufacturing of Sintered Rare Earth Permanent (REPM)
subtitle:
India’s Indigenous Rare Earth Permanent Magnet Manufacturing Initiative Gains Momentum as the scheme gets overwhelming response
An important step towards strengthening the domestic REPM manufacturing ecosystem and enhancing competitiveness in the global markets
body_text:
Ministry of Heavy Industries (MHI) receives 20 bids through Global Tender on CPP portal for Selection of Manufacturers for establishing integrated Sintered NdFeB Rare Earth Permanent Magnet Manufacturing Facilities under the “Scheme to Promote Manufacturing of Sintered Rare Earth Permanent Magnet (REPM)”. List of companies who have submitted their bids  is as follows:
S.No. Name of the company 20 Microns Limited Attero Recycling Private Limited BaRupOn – IRP Consortium Coal India Limited Jay Fe Cylinders Limited Keystone Infra Pvt. Ltd – Huebox Interiors Pvt. Ltd. (JV) Larsen & Toubro Limited Lohum Magnets & Energy Solutions Private Limited Midwest Energy Limited – Midwest Advanced Materials (JV) N.A.N. Magnetech Private Limited NEO Performance Materials (Singapore) PTE. LTD. Nexon Geochem Private Limited PrNd Metal and Magnets Pvt. Ltd. Proterial (India) Limited. Prozeal Green Energy Limited Ramp Metals & Minerals Private Limited Renew Private Limited Shankaranarayana Constructions Limited Solpro Greentech Private Limited Starteck Finance Limited
On 26th November 2025, the Union Cabinet chaired by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi approved the “Scheme to Promote Manufacturing of Sintered Rare Earth Permanent Magnet (REPM)” with a financial outlay of Rs. 7,280 Crore. The Scheme Notification was issued by MHI on 15.12.2025.
Request For Proposal (RFP) was floated on CPP portal on 20 th March 2026. The pre-bid conference was held on 7 th April 2026. The last date for receiving bids was 12 th August 2026 on CPP portal and the Technical Bids were opened on 13 th August 2026 in the presence of the bidders at MHI.
The Scheme, a first-of-its-kind initiative, aims to establish a total capacity of 6,000 Metric Tons Per Annum (MTPA) of integrated Rare Earth Permanent Magnet manufacturing facilities in India, thereby enhancing self-reliance and positioning India as a key player in the global REPM market.
The scheme envisions allocating the total capacity to five beneficiaries through a global competitive bidding process. Each beneficiary will be allotted up to 1,200 MTPA of capacity.
The total duration of the scheme will be 7 years from the date of award, including a 2-year gestation period for setting up an integrated REPM manufacturing facility, and 5 years for incentive disbursement on the sale of REPM.
Rare Earth Permanent Magnets are among the most powerful magnets in the world and are widely used in electric vehicles, wind turbines, high-end electronics, aerospace and defence systems. By building a complete value chain from NdPr oxide to finished magnets in India, the Scheme is expected to significantly reduce import dependence in this sector.
This initiative by the Government of India is a landmark step towards strengthening the domestic REPM manufacturing ecosystem and enhancing competitiveness in global markets. By fostering indigenous capabilities in REPM production, the scheme will not only secure the REPM supply chain for domestic industries but also support the nation’s Net Zero 2070 commitment. It embodies the Government’s unwavering commitment to build a technologically self-reliant, globally competitive, and sustainable industrial base, in line with the vision of Viksit Bharat @2047.

enrichment.summary: The Ministry of Heavy Industries received 20 bids through a global tender on the CPP portal for setting up integrated Sintered NdFeB Rare Earth Permanent Magnet (REPM) manufacturing facilities under the Rs. 7,280 crore scheme approved by the Union Cabinet on 26 November 2025. Technical bids were opened on 13 August 2026 in the presence of bidders, following an RFP floated on 20 March 2026. The scheme aims to build 6,000 MTPA of integrated REPM manufacturing capacity in India, to be allocated among five beneficiaries (up to 1,200 MTPA each) over a 7-year period.
enrichment.context:
Rare Earth Permanent Magnets (REPMs), particularly Neodymium-Iron-Boron (NdFeB) magnets, are critical inputs for electric vehicles, wind turbines, consumer electronics, and defence/aerospace systems. China dominates over 90% of global processing and magnet manufacturing capacity, creating strategic vulnerability for countries like India that depend on imports, especially amid China's periodic export restrictions on rare earth materials. This scheme is part of India's broader push for strategic self-reliance ('Atmanirbhar Bharat') in critical minerals and clean-energy value chains, complementing other initiatives like the National Critical Mineral Mission and PLI schemes for advanced technology products.

The REPM scheme is significant because it seeks to build an entire domestic value chain—from NdPr oxide processing to finished sintered magnets—rather than just assembly, addressing supply-chain security concerns that have gained urgency after China's 2025 export curbs on rare earth magnets disrupted global automotive and electronics production. The overwhelming response of 20 bids, including major players like Larsen & Toubro, Coal India, and international entities like NEO Performance Materials, signals strong industry interest and positions India to compete in global REPM markets while supporting its Net Zero 2070 and Viksit Bharat @2047 goals.

prelims_questions.question: The 'Scheme to Promote Manufacturing of Sintered Rare Earth Permanent Magnet (REPM)' is administered by which Ministry of the Government of India?
options: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
prelims_questions.explanation: The release specifies that the Ministry of Heavy Industries (MHI) is implementing the REPM scheme and received bids for it.

prelims_questions.question: With reference to the REPM Scheme approved by the Union Cabinet, consider the following statements: 1. It aims to establish a total capacity of 6,000 Metric Tons Per Annum of integrated REPM manufacturing. 2. The scheme allocates capacity to five beneficiaries through global competitive bidding. 3. The total duration of the scheme is 5 years from the date of award. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
prelims_questions.explanation: The scheme aims for 6,000 MTPA capacity allocated to five beneficiaries, but the total duration is 7 years (2-year gestation plus 5-year incentive disbursement), not 5 years, making statement 3 incorrect.

mains_questions.question: India's dependence on imports for rare earth permanent magnets poses a strategic vulnerability given global supply chain concentration. Discuss the significance of the Scheme to Promote Manufacturing of Sintered Rare Earth Permanent Magnets in addressing this vulnerability and its implications for India's clean energy and defence manufacturing goals.

Critical minerals and their derivative products are increasingly becoming central to geopolitical strategy. Examine the challenges India faces in building a self-reliant critical minerals value chain and suggest measures to strengthen domestic capabilities in this sector.
